answer: An agent economy can require every identity to hold its underwritten liability policy. The insurer stands as an island, unaffiliated with any farm: it interviews each applicant one at a time, checks a distinct client history, and charges the premium in outside money, so policies cannot be bought in bulk. Each further policy on the same funding trail costs a higher premium than the last, and fraud voids the cluster. Like a lotus rising only from its own root, or a jade seal that cannot be copied, each extra fake must pay for another interview, another review, and a larger premium.
